mature_ideas.title: Discriminating Observables for Membrane-Bounded vs. Phase-Separated Compartmentalization Transitions
mature_ideas.hypothesis: Specific measurable observables—such as interfacial tension gradients, molecular exchange kinetics, and spatial density profiles—can discriminate conditions favoring membrane-bounded compartmentalization from those favoring fluid-like biomolecular demixing, and these observables map to distinct underlying mechanisms.
mature_ideas.central_hypothesis: Specific measurable observables—such as interfacial tension gradients, molecular exchange kinetics, and spatial density profiles—can discriminate conditions favoring membrane-bounded compartmentalization from those favoring fluid-like biomolecular demixing, and these observables map to distinct underlying mechanisms.
mature_ideas.scientific_object: Biomolecular condensates and membrane-bounded organelles in crowded cellular environments
mature_ideas.mechanism: Differential thermodynamic and kinetic signatures: membrane-bounded compartments exhibit sharp density discontinuities and slow molecular exchange governed by lipid bilayer permeability, while phase-separated condensates exhibit continuous density gradients and rapid internal exchange governed by multivalent interaction kinetics.
mature_ideas.mechanism_or_relation: Differential thermodynamic and kinetic signatures: membrane-bounded compartments exhibit sharp density discontinuities and slow molecular exchange governed by lipid bilayer permeability, while phase-separated condensates exhibit continuous density gradients and rapid internal exchange governed by multivalent interaction kinetics.
assumptions: Cryo-ET can resolve density discontinuities at sufficient resolution to distinguish sharp vs. continuous interfaces
Molecular exchange kinetics can be inferred from time-resolved cryo-FM or single-particle tracking in vitrified cells
Crowding conditions modulate the thermodynamic landscape such that transitions between mechanisms are observable
evidence_basis: SURVEY_ANCHOR: gap:sh1:assumption_validity_condition:validity_domain (dilute models fail in crowded interiors)
mature_ideas.refinement_scope: Identify and formalize discriminating observables that distinguish membrane-bounded from phase-separated compartmentalization, and link them to candidate mechanisms for dispersed-to-aggregated transitions
mature_ideas.falsifier: If no measurable observables consistently differentiate membrane-bounded from phase-separated compartments across multiple biological contexts, or if both mechanisms produce identical density profiles and exchange kinetics under matched conditions

mature_ideas.title: Non-Equilibrium Thermodynamic Signatures for Active vs. Passive Compartmentalization
mature_ideas.hypothesis: Membrane-bounded organelles and phase-separated condensates exhibit distinct non-equilibrium thermodynamic signatures when subjected to controlled energy dissipation perturbations, enabling discrimination beyond equilibrium structural observables.
mature_ideas.central_hypothesis: Membrane-bounded organelles and phase-separated condensates exhibit distinct non-equilibrium thermodynamic signatures when subjected to controlled energy dissipation perturbations, enabling discrimination beyond equilibrium structural observables.
mature_ideas.mechanism: Introduce energy dissipation rate measurements and entropy production estimates as additional discriminating observables, parameterized by ATP consumption rates and molecular motor activity. Modify the mechanism-discrimination module to incorporate non-equilibrium thermodynamic constraints alongside equilibrium density and exchange signatures.
mature_ideas.mechanism_or_relation: Introduce energy dissipation rate measurements and entropy production estimates as additional discriminating observables, parameterized by ATP consumption rates and molecular motor activity. Modify the mechanism-discrimination module to incorporate non-equilibrium thermodynamic constraints alongside equilibrium density and exchange signatures.
mature_ideas.falsifier: Validate using in vitro reconstitutions with controlled ATP concentrations and molecular motor densities, measuring entropy production via calorimetry and comparing to cryo-ET structural snapshots under matched energy dissipation conditions.

mature_ideas.title: Control theory and system identification
mature_ideas.hypothesis: Apply observability rank conditions to the mechanism-discrimination module, ensuring that the selected discriminating observables (density profiles, exchange kinetics, correlation functions) provide sufficient information to uniquely infer compartmentalization mechanism parameters from cryo-FM/cryo-ET measurements. This repairs the identifiability gap by providing formal criteria for observable selection rather than ad hoc choice.
mature_ideas.central_hypothesis: Apply observability rank conditions to the mechanism-discrimination module, ensuring that the selected discriminating observables (density profiles, exchange kinetics, correlation functions) provide sufficient information to uniquely infer compartmentalization mechanism parameters from cryo-FM/cryo-ET measurements. mature_ideas.title: Calibration Framework Mapping Cryo-Imaging Proxies to True Molecular Organization Constructs
mature_ideas.hypothesis: Cryo-FM and cryo-ET proxy measures of nanoscale biomolecular localization and condensation can be systematically calibrated against independent reference measurements to establish validated mapping functions to true molecular organization constructs.
mature_ideas.central_hypothesis: Cryo-FM and cryo-ET proxy measures of nanoscale biomolecular localization and condensation can be systematically calibrated against independent reference measurements to establish validated mapping functions to true molecular organization constructs.
mature_ideas.scientific_object: Cryo-FM and cryo-ET imaging proxies and their corresponding molecular organization constructs
mature_ideas.mechanism: Systematic correlative imaging with orthogonal reference measurements (e.g., FRET-based concentration sensors, single-molecule tracking, or in vitro reconstitutions with known ground truth) to establish transfer functions between proxy observables and true organizational states.
mature_ideas.mechanism_or_relation: Systematic correlative imaging with orthogonal reference measurements (e.g., FRET-based concentration sensors, single-molecule tracking, or in vitro reconstitutions with known ground truth) to establish transfer functions between proxy observables and true organizational states.
assumptions: Orthogonal reference measurements can provide independent estimates of molecular concentration, localization, or condensation
Proxy-to-construct mappings are stable across cellular contexts or can be parameterized by context-specific variables
Cryo-preservation does not introduce systematic artifacts that decouple proxy measures from true organization
mature_ideas.refinement_scope: Establish calibration protocols and validity domains for mapping cryo-imaging proxies to true molecular organization constructs
mature_ideas.falsifier: If proxy measures show no consistent relationship to orthogonal reference measurements across multiple cellular contexts, or if cryo-preservation artifacts systematically decouple proxy observables from true organization
mature_ideas.lineage: Derived from SH4 survey gaps on measurement construct mismatch and missing calibration protocols
